title: Electrical standards network
question: How do fixed h and e connect exact present International System of Units (SI) electrical identities, bounded charge and voltage calculations, and historical 1990 conventional values?
predictionPrompt: Choose whether exact, input-dependent, and historical nodes remain distinct; the Josephson view can evaluate both f = K_J V and V = f/K_J from separate stated inputs.
sourceRevision: PHYSICS_TOUR_MASTER_PLAN.md, 2026-07-26 contract; BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment; CIPM 1988 conventional values effective 1990
sourceLocator: Chapter 6 standards network; fixed h and e; K_J-90 and R_K-90 historical comparison layer
caveats: Exact ideal relationships do not make practical electrical realizations uncertainty-free.
K_J-90 and R_K-90 are historical conventional values and are not current exact SI substitutions.
The carrier count is not a Hall filling factor or conductance-channel count.

numericalMethod.name: Exact identity network with bounded inputs
numericalMethod.description: Evaluates the fixed h/e identity network, one integer carrier count, bounded voltage and Josephson-frequency inputs, and two signed historical comparisons once.

modelComponents.label: Current SI electrical identity network
modelComponents.description: Derives K_J, R_K, G_0, Phi_0, and the joule value of eV from the fixed exact SI values of h and e.

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
attribution.sourceLocator: Fixed h and e and exact quantum electrical relationships
caveats: Identity exactness is separate from practical device realization uncertainty.

modelComponents.label: Bounded charge and voltage calculation
modelComponents.description: Uses an integer carrier count to form q = N e and a supplied voltage to form E = N e V; the Josephson view maps V to f = K_J V and an independently supplied f to V = f/K_J.

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; tour-electrical-standards-v1 contract
caveats: The calculation uses charge magnitude and omits sign, junction dynamics, and Hall-device state.

modelComponents.label: Historical 1990 conventional comparison
modelComponents.description: Retains K_J-90 and R_K-90 as separate historical nodes and compares each with the corresponding current exact SI relationship.

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment; CIPM 1988 conventional values effective 1990
attribution.sourceLocator: CIPM Recommendations 1 and 2 (CI-1988) and revised-SI comparison
caveats: Historical conventional values are never substituted for current exact SI values.

equations: q = N e; E = q V; 1 eV = e J
assumptions: chargeCarriers is an integer count used only for total charge and voltage-dependent carrier energy.
The ideal Josephson and quantum Hall relationships remain separate from practical device realization.
The supplied voltage is finite and within [0, 1e6] V.
The supplied Josephson frequency is finite and within [0, 1e15] Hz; it is active only in the Josephson view.
K_J-90 and R_K-90 are retained only as historical conventional comparison values.
No calibration certificate, device correction, Hall plateau, or uncertainty dataset is loaded.

controls.label: Standards view
controls.description: Selects the single-electron, Josephson, or quantum Hall view recognized by the electrical standards engine.
controls.playfulPrompt: Choose which path through h and e to highlight.

options.label: Single electron
options.description: inspect one elementary charge and its voltage-dependent energy

options.label: Josephson relation
options.description: trace K_J and the ideal voltage-to-frequency relationship

options.label: Quantum Hall relation
options.description: trace R_K while keeping practical plateau realization separate

controls.label: Charge-carrier count
controls.description: Supplies the engine's bounded integer N for q = N e; it is not a Hall filling factor or channel count.
controls.playfulPrompt: Count charge magnitudes without assigning a device state.

controls.label: Applied voltage
controls.description: Supplies a bounded voltage for E = N e V and, in the Josephson view, f = K_J V.
controls.playfulPrompt: Predict the input-dependent nodes before the network updates.

controls.label: Josephson frequency
controls.description: Supplies bounded cyclic frequency f for V = f/K_J in the Josephson view; zero is the inactive placeholder in complete non-Josephson presets.

presets.label: Single electron at one volt
presets.description: Inspect one elementary charge and the exact joule value of one electron volt.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Which nodes are exact identities, and which one depends on the selected voltage?

presets.label: Josephson voltage path
presets.description: Trace two charge magnitudes, K_J, the ideal frequency associated with one millivolt, and the ideal voltage associated with 70 GHz.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Compare f = K_J V with V = f/K_J, then explain why exact K_J does not certify a practical junction realization.

presets.label: Quantum Hall identity path
presets.description: Highlight R_K and G_0 while retaining the historical R_K-90 comparison as a separate node.
presets.inspectionPrompt: What device evidence would still be needed to claim a resistance realization?

outputSchema.label: Total charge magnitude
outputSchema.description: The bounded input calculation q = N e.

outputSchema.label: Carrier energy magnitude
outputSchema.description: The voltage-dependent magnitude E = N e V; null only when no voltage input is supplied.

outputSchema.label: Josephson frequency from voltage
outputSchema.description: The ideal f = K_J V result in the Josephson view; null in the other views.

outputSchema.label: Josephson voltage from frequency
outputSchema.description: The ideal V = f/K_J result from the Technical frequency input in the Josephson view; null in the other views.

outputSchema.label: K_J-90 relative difference
outputSchema.description: One million times (K_J-90 - K_J)/K_J, with positive sign when the historical value is larger.

outputSchema.label: R_K-90 relative difference
outputSchema.description: One million times (R_K-90 - R_K)/R_K, with negative sign when the historical value is smaller.

outputSchema.label: Network status summary
outputSchema.description: Distinguishes exact defining SI, exact derived SI, input-dependent, and historical-conventional-1990 nodes.

comparison.incompatibleBehavior: Render standards networks in parallel without merging nodes or historical differences when simulation revision or output schema differs.

visualization.description: Shows h and e feeding exact present-SI identity nodes, bounded input-dependent nodes, and separate historical 1990 conventional comparison nodes.

alternatives.description: A sentence reports the selected standards view, bounded inputs, exact identity values, input calculations, historical signed differences, and realization caveats.
A table lists each network node with symbol, value, unit, status label, and note, followed by the historical comparison rows.

visualization.reducedMotionBehavior: Render the complete electrical standards network immediately without animated edge tracing or node movement.

finding.changed: At runtime, the standards view, integer carrier count, bounded voltage, and Technical Josephson frequency change only the highlighted and input-dependent portions of the fixed identity network.
finding.cause: Fixed exact SI h and e determine K_J, R_K, G_0, Phi_0, and eV algebraically; N, V, and f determine charge, energy, and the two Josephson conversions.
finding.equation: K_J = 2e/h; R_K = h/e^2; G_0 = 2e^2/h; Phi_0 = h/(2e); q = N e; E = q V; f = K_J V; V = f/K_J
assumptions: N is an integer count used only for charge magnitude and voltage-dependent energy
Ideal quantum electrical relationships are separate from practical realization
K_J-90 and R_K-90 remain historical comparison values
finding.establishes: For an evaluated input, the exact h/e identity network, bounded charge and voltage calculations, and both signed historical relative differences.
finding.doesNotEstablish: Device accuracy, uncertainty-free realization, a Josephson step condition, a quantized Hall plateau, a Hall filling factor, a conductance-channel count, or empirical validation.
finding.sourceRevision: tour-electrical-standards-v1 contract; BIPM SI Brochure 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment; CIPM 1988 conventional values effective 1990
finding.sourceLocator: Electrical standards evaluation, node, edge, and historical comparison contract
caveats: Exact current SI relationships and practical device realizations have distinct uncertainty statements.
Historical relative differences use (conventional - current exact SI)/current exact SI.
The carrier count is not interpreted as a Hall or transport-state parameter.
